rows.notes: Narrative literature review (labelled 'Review'; Section 1 and 6 describe the paper as a review of smart irrigation monitoring and control strategies). Reports no own data; water-saving figures in Tables 1-2 are compiled from cited studies (e.g. Liao et al. 2021, Abioye et al. 2021), which do not count as the study's own result.

Review paper with no own experiment, survey or model runs. Yield effects of smart irrigation are only mentioned via cited work (e.g. Montesano et al. 2016 in Table 2); no own evidence on yield maintenance.

Review paper; no primary data. Drip irrigation is not the subject of the review (it concerns monitoring and control strategies); drip appears only incidentally in cited studies (Mill<U+00E1>n et al. 2019, Sudarmaji et al. 2019).

Review paper. The hybrid model predictive control with combined soil/plant/weather sensors is proposed in Section 5 and the Conclusions as future work ('needs to be evaluated in an open field'); the authors explicitly state the impact on water use efficiency is not known. No own result.
Review paper with no own data. Smartphone apps and user-friendly control panels are not discussed in the review; water-saving statements are drawn from cited literature only.
Review paper with no own data. Soil health is not addressed anywhere in the text; the review concerns soil moisture monitoring and irrigation control for water use efficiency.
Review paper; no own evidence on agricultural productivity. Climate change is mentioned only as background motivation in the Introduction.

Review paper; no own data. Drought resilience or climate change mitigation by smart irrigation scheduling is not examined; drought indices are mentioned only in the abstract/introduction as motivation.
Review paper. Section 3.1 describes soil moisture sensors and cites other studies' findings; no own measurements or yield results.
Review paper. Water savings attributed to soil moisture sensing in Table 1 (e.g. 30%, 50%, 58.8%) are all figures reported by cited studies, not the review's own result.
Review paper describing soil-, weather- and plant-based monitoring integration (Sections 3 and 5) conceptually and via cited work; no own evidence of water-use reduction.
Review paper; no own data on crop productivity. Authors state that the impact of MPC-based control on water productivity is not known and propose it for future research.
The passage accurately characterises the paper as a review emphasising advanced control strategies, but a review provides no primary evidence on the claimed effect.
Review paper. Section 4 argues from literature that closed-loop control copes with uncertainty better than open-loop systems; this is a narrative conclusion, not an own result.
Review paper; the passage correctly describes it as presenting adaptive/closed-loop control as a route to improved water use efficiency, but the paper has no own data.

Review paper; no own evidence. The review does not actually make the specific point about 'precautionary over-application driven by limited visibility'; it discusses over/under-irrigation under open-loop control generally.
Review paper; no own data. The review does not discuss farmers reallocating saved water or expanding irrigated area; the claimed rebound mechanism is not in this text.

Review paper; no own evidence. It does note from literature that controller performance depends on data representativeness (ANN) and designer expertise (fuzzy), but these are narrative points, not own findings.
Review paper; no own data. Risk management as such is not addressed; the review discusses avoiding plant stress and handling uncertainty conceptually.

notes: The cited document is a narrative literature review (Bwambale et al. 2022, Agric. Water Manag.) of smart irrigation monitoring and control strategies. It reports no original experiment, survey, measurement or validated model run; all quantitative findings in Tables 1 and 2 are compiled from cited studies. Hence Q1 is 'no' for every claim row and Q2-Q9 follow as 'no'. Full text appears complete (abstract through references).
